title: Module quiz: Reliability of multi-agent systems

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario: Dovetail Labs sets a breaker threshold of three consecutive failures for each agent. Agent X fails, succeeds, fails, succeeds, and fails again. Agent Y fails three times running. Which breakers are open afterwards?

options.text: Only Y's, since X's tally returns to zero whenever a call works
options.says: The count is of consecutive failures, and a success clears it.

options.text: Both, since each agent has failed at least three times in all across the run
options.says: Ruled out because "The count is of consecutive failures for one agent, not of all failures in the run".

options.text: Only X's, since it has made the larger number of calls overall in the run
options.says: Ruled out because "A success resets the count, so scattered failures do not open it".

options.text: Neither, because a breaker opens only after a cooldown has already passed
options.says: Ruled out because the breaker opens "After a set number of failures in a row", and the cooldown comes after it opens.

origin.section: A circuit breaker stops the spending

questions.stem: Scenario: Larkspur Media's runner wraps every task in a catch-all that records any exception as a failure and carries on. A coding defect makes task seven raise an unexpected error in every run. What is wrong with this design?

options.text: Nothing, because carrying on always gives the most complete report that is possible
options.says: Ruled out because "The runner handles failures it expects", and anything else is a crash that must not be caught.

options.text: It should retry the task until the error stops, since all errors are temporary ones
options.says: Ruled out because "an unlimited retry is a way to spend money while nothing changes".

options.text: It presents a software bug as routine trouble, so the real fault stays hidden
options.says: An unexpected error is a defect, and catching it as a routine failure hides it.

options.text: It should delete the stored results so that the next run starts again from nothing
options.says: Ruled out because "the crash still loses nothing finished", so deleting the stored results destroys what the checkpoint protects.

origin.section: A crash is not a failure

questions.stem: Scenario: Hazel Analytics' plan has tasks a, b, c and d, where d needs b. In the first run b used up its retries, and a and c finished and were saved. What does a second run call?

options.text: All four, since a run restarts the whole plan
options.says: Ruled out because "a second run does only the work that is left".

options.text: Only b, since a skipped task is not retried later
options.says: Ruled out because "Failures, skips and degraded answers are not stored, because a later run must be free to try them again".

options.text: b, then d, since a and c come from the checkpoint
options.says: The second run does the failed task and the one that was skipped because of it, and takes the rest from the checkpoint.

options.text: Just d, since b is known to have failed in the earlier run
options.says: Ruled out because d needs b, and the remaining work is "the task that failed, the tasks that were skipped because of it, and nothing else".
